relevance_note: National survey describing 54 individually tabulated HA20 patients: "All 54 patients analyzed had heterozygous variants in TNFAIP3".
method_note:
Read the whole paper including the converted supplement. Supplementary Tables 1 and 2 (HTML) were transcribed by a Python script that kept raw character offsets, so each table span is an exact substring running from the patient label through the cell (HTML tags and line breaks included verbatim). I checked the script output against both tables (54 rows each); the '+' counts match main-text Table 2 for recurrent fever (46), oral ulcer/recurrent stomatitis (42), intestinal symptoms (41), musculoskeletal (20) and autoimmune disease (15), and sex is 25 M / 29 F. HTML entities (>) and Markdown escapes (\>) are decoded in values only, never in spans. Labels: P1-P54 and family labels F1-F37 as printed in Supplementary Tables 1-2.
Table symbols: '+' in a feature column was read as present. The paper never defines '−' or '-', so those cells are 'not reported' and no excluded rows come from the tables; empty cells are 'not reported'. An IFN score of 'Normal' is recorded as an excluded 'elevated IFN score'. Treatment cells with '-' were not interpreted. The 'Initial diagnosis' column was not used as phenotype evidence, because these are diagnoses at presentation and some were revised (e.g. 'IgA vasculitis→SLE, SS'). 'Intestinal symptoms' was not mapped to the checklist item 'gastrointestinal ulcers or inflammation' (broader term; the Table 3 endoscopy counts are not per patient). 'HD' was read as Hashimoto's disease although the legend defines 'HS, Hashimoto’s disease' (HS never appears; the 8 HD entries match 'Hashimoto’s disease (8)').
Conservative checklist choices: no mapping for Graves' disease (autoimmune thyroiditis), Hodgkin's/malignant lymphoma (lymphoproliferation), Kawasaki disease (vasculitis), posterior iris adhesions or eyelid conjunctival aphthae (ocular inflammation), core ataxia/headache/psychiatric symptoms (CNS; the paper names only patients 10, 33, 38, 44 and 47 as CNS involvement), or 'AIH susp' (P53, suspected only). No exclusion was inferred from group statements: 'CNS involvement was observed in 5 patients' and 'Pulmonary disease was observed in three patients' name the positives but are count statements, and other patients have neurological symptoms. Ethnicity 'Japanese' for all except P51 comes from 'Fifty-three of the patients were Japanese and one was Vietnamese (patient 51)'. P3 was identified as the Discussion's 'our patient' treated with HCT (the only HCT patient), giving the GI-lesion and lung rows. PFAPA symptoms for P20 come from 'the former two cases' (patients 20 and 11).
Other in-scope people: mother of P3 and father of P18 (low-level somatic TNFAIP3 mosaicism, 10.06% and 16.7%; variant not printed; asymptomatic; checklist left 'not reported' rather than mapping 'asymptomatic' item by item); father of P38 (HA20) and grandmother of P15 (suspected HA20), each with malignant lymphoma, onset ages 35 and 70 years assigned by 'respectively'; no variant row because none is tied to them. Unnamed person 1 = excluded case with 22% mosaic c.806-1G>T; unnamed person 2 = excluded case with 14% mosaic p.Q760X and Behcet's-like symptoms; plus that person's two symptomatic family members, who did not carry the variant (no variant rows). No rows for: the 20 excluded missense cases (group level only; Supplementary Table 6 lists 16 variants without people), the three asymptomatic heterozygous carriers (count only), non-analysed relatives in Supplementary Figure 1 (figure only), and the rest of the estimated 72 patients. The trailing '(3)' after 'father of patient 18' may cite an earlier report; main-text reference numbers (e.g. (3), (20)) refer to a list that is not in this file. prior_report_citation lists the per-patient 'reference' column of Supplementary Table 1 (numbers as printed).
Variant type was read from the printed notation only where it names the class (fs = frameshift, X = nonsense), from the text for missense (p.E192K, p.C243Y) and splice (minigene variants; c.2088+5G>C via 'exon 8 skipping'), and from 'deletion' in the cell for CNVs. c.1906+1G>A was left 'not reported'. Cytobands were not recorded as genomic coordinates. cohort_size_as_stated = 54 analysed (the authors estimate 72 HA20 patients in Japan).
Contradictions in the paper: (1) P49: Supplementary Table 1 and the minigene section give c.2088+1G>A, but the main text says 'patient 49 (c.2099 + 1G>A)'; recorded c.2088+1G>A. (2) Supplement Methods list 'c.986+1G\>T' among the minigene constructs, while the results, figure legend and Table 1 give c.986+1G>C (P50 recorded as c.986+1G>C). (3) Genital ulcer '+' count is 20 in Supplementary Table 2 vs 'Genital ulcer 19' in Table 2; cutaneous entries are 26 vs 'Cutaneous symptoms 27'. (4) Methods say HA20 was 'confirmed via functional analysis of the TNFAIP3 variant', but the supplement excludes large deletions and known variants from the reporter assay (P24, P27, P28, P38 and P54 carry deletions). Not transcribed: Supplementary Table 3 (anti-drug antibodies), HLA results, figure-only content.
